symptom: `mxcli check -p app.mpr bad.mdl good.mdl` exits 1 but its last line is "Check passed!"; reversing the file order flips the last line, so anything reading the log tail sees success
cause: `runCheckFiles` ran `runCheckFileAgainst` per file and kept only the worst exit code; each file prints its own verdict and nothing printed one for the set, so the last file's "Check passed!" (plus its no-project note) closed the run
insight: A per-unit verdict line is read as the run's verdict by whoever tails the log (agents especially); when a command loops over inputs, the loop owner must print the aggregate last. The per-file "Check passed!" is followed by the two-line no-project note, so assert on the true last line rather than `Contains`, or the test passes against the bug. No project needed for the test: a syntax error makes the failing file
